title: Tensoring a quasi-coherent module by an invertible module
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then for every integer $n$, the tensor product $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ (with negative powers defined using the dual invertible module) is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MR affine case; quasi-coherence of tensor products with invertible modules

proof.text: The zero tensor power is $\mathcal O_Y$, hence is locally free of rank one and invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module]. The dual $\mathcal L^\vee$ is invertible by [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible]. For $n>0$, induction on $n$ using the tensor-product clause of that same lemma shows that $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is invertible. For $n<0$, apply the same induction to $(\mathcal L^\vee)^{\otimes(-n)}$, which is the specified negative power. Thus every integer tensor power in the statement is invertible.

source.place: lemma lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible, statement; induction on the tensor exponent

proof.text: For each integer $n$, Step 1 makes $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ invertible, hence quasi-coherent by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Apply the quasi-coherent tensor-product clause of [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-tensor-product-affine-sections] to $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ on $Y$. Its conclusion is precisely that $\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is quasi-coherent.
